chapters.summary: Solomon offers sacrifices at Gibeon and asks God for wisdom; God grants him unmatched wisdom and wealth to govern Israel.
keyPoints: Solomon and the whole assembly go up to the high place at Gibeon to offer sacrifices and seek the LORD.
God appears to Solomon in a dream and promises to give him wisdom and wealth.
Solomon buys horses from Egypt and amasses great wealth, strengthening the kingdom.
chapters.application: Let us follow Solomon's example and seek first God's kingdom and his righteousness, and God will surely supply all we need.

chapters.summary: Solomon prepares materials for building the temple and asks Hiram king of Tyre to supply cedar timber and skilled craftsmen, emphasizing the temple's grandeur and God's transcendence.
keyPoints: Solomon assembles seventy thousand carriers, eighty thousand stonecutters, and thirty-six hundred overseers to prepare materials for the temple.
Solomon asks Hiram king of Tyre for cedar timber and skilled craftsmen, explaining the purpose of the temple.
Solomon declares that though the temple is magnificent, God is far greater than the heavens, and building it is only to burn incense and offer sacrifice before him.
chapters.application: Let us prepare wholeheartedly for God's work, yet remain humble, for God is far beyond anything we can imagine, and every work should ultimately bring him glory.

chapters.summary: Solomon builds the temple in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, adorning it carefully according to the pattern God gave, displaying his glory.
keyPoints: Solomon begins building the temple on Mount Moriah, and its foundation is laid.
The interior of the temple is decorated with pure gold and precious stones, of surpassing splendor.
The cherubim and the veil symbolize God's presence, and the most holy place reveals his holiness.
chapters.application: Today let us worship God in spirit and in truth, letting him reign in our lives, so that our lives become a temple of glory.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how Solomon made the bronze altar, the bronze sea, the stands, and various furnishings for the temple, completing its decoration and equipping.
keyPoints: The bronze altar and the bronze sea are made, symbolizing worship and cleansing.
Ten stands and bronze basins are made for washing the offerings.
The gold lampstands, tables, and gold bowls display God's glory.
chapters.application: Let us worship God with a pure heart, glorifying him in every detail of our lives, and prepare ourselves to become a temple of the Holy Spirit.

chapters.summary: Solomon brings the vessels and the ark of the covenant into the temple, and the glory of the LORD fills the house.
keyPoints: Solomon assembles the elders of Israel and the heads of all the tribes and brings the ark up from the city of David into the temple.
The Levites carry the ark, the priests offer sacrifices, and the people sound trumpets and sing praises to the LORD.
After the ark is set in place, a cloud fills the temple and the glory of the LORD appears, so that the priests cannot stand to minister.
chapters.application: When God's presence draws near, let us stand in awe, responding with worship and obedience, so that he may reign in our lives.

chapters.summary: At the dedication of the temple, Solomon offers a prayer to God, asking him to hear the prayers Israel offers toward the temple.
keyPoints: Solomon declares that the temple is finished and that God's covenant with David is fulfilled.
Solomon kneels before the altar and lifts his hands toward heaven in prayer.
Solomon asks God to watch over the temple day and night and to hear the pleas of his people.
chapters.application: Let us follow Solomon's example, remembering God's promises in prayer, seeking his presence, and trusting that he will surely hear our cries.

chapters.summary: After Solomon dedicates the temple, the LORD appears to him by night, answers his prayer, and warns the people that unfaithfulness will bring punishment.
keyPoints: The glory of the LORD fills the temple, and the people bow down and worship, giving thanks that the LORD is good.
Solomon and the people offer abundant sacrifices and keep the feast for seven days, rejoicing over the temple's dedication.
God appears by night and answers Solomon's prayer, but warns that disaster will come if they forsake him.
chapters.application: Let us worship God with thankful hearts, while remembering his warnings and remaining faithful; if we stray, let us humbly repent and experience his forgiveness and restoration.

chapters.summary: Solomon completes the temple, the palace, and other projects, and following David's instructions offers sacrifices according to the law and organizes the priests and Levites into their divisions.
keyPoints: Solomon builds and completes the house of the LORD and the royal palace, along with cities such as Gezer and Lower Beth-horon.
Following David's instructions, Solomon establishes the divisions of the priests and Levites, and keeps the appointed feasts and offerings.
Besides Pharaoh's daughter, Solomon also marries foreign women from the Hittites, the Amorites, and other nations.
chapters.application: Let us obey God's commands in everything, keep worship at the center of our lives, and choose our life partners carefully, lest we be led away from the true path.

chapters.summary: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon and marvels at his wisdom and wealth; Solomon becomes exceedingly rich, and at last he dies.
keyPoints: Hearing of Solomon's wisdom, the Queen of Sheba comes to test him with hard questions, and seeing his palace, his officials, and his wisdom, she is left breathless with amazement.
Solomon receives 666 talents of gold each year, becoming the wealthiest man on earth, and nations everywhere bring tribute to hear his wisdom.
After reigning forty years, Solomon dies, and his son Rehoboam succeeds him, and the kingdom enters a new era.
chapters.application: Let us seek heavenly wisdom rather than worldly wealth; let us receive God's gifts with humility and use our resources well to glorify him.

chapters.summary: Rehoboam rejects the counsel of the elders, and Israel splits apart, fulfilling the word God spoke through Ahijah.
keyPoints: The people of Israel ask for their heavy yoke to be lightened, and Rehoboam first consults the old men and then the young men.
Rehoboam follows the advice of the young men and answers the people harshly.
Israel rebels against the house of David and makes Jeroboam king, and Judah and Israel are divided.
chapters.application: When making decisions, let us humbly seek wisdom and listen to the counsel of our elders, avoiding pride and self-reliance. May the Lord give us humble, teachable hearts, that we may follow his will and enjoy his peace.

chapters.summary: Rehoboam obeys God's word and does not attack Israel; he fortifies cities, and priests and Levites come over to him, and his household grows large.
keyPoints: Rehoboam listens to God's word and gives up his plan to attack the northern kingdom of Israel.
Rehoboam builds up the cities of Judah, strengthening its defenses and securing his rule.
The priests and Levites, rejected by Jeroboam, come over to Judah and strengthen Rehoboam.
chapters.application: When facing conflict, let us first inquire of God and submit to his guidance; and let us remain faithful to our beliefs, for God will surely grant peace and strength.

chapters.summary: Because Rehoboam forsakes the LORD, Shishak king of Egypt attacks him; after Rehoboam repents, God relents from destroying them, though they must serve the king of Egypt, showing both God's justice and his mercy.
keyPoints: Once Rehoboam is established and strong, he forsakes the LORD, and the people follow him into sin, bringing on God's discipline.
Shishak king of Egypt attacks Jerusalem; the prophet Shemaiah delivers God's word, and Rehoboam humbles himself and repents.
Seeing their repentance, God does not destroy them completely, though he leaves them to serve the king of Egypt, and still grants them some measure of deliverance.
chapters.application: In times of ease we easily grow proud and drift from God; when discipline comes, let us humbly repent, for God will surely relent and show mercy, leaving room for grace.

chapters.summary: Abijah king of Judah fights against Jeroboam king of Israel, and because he relies on the LORD he wins a great victory, showing that God is with the house of David.
keyPoints: Before the battle Abijah declares that God made a covenant of salt with the house of David, and rebukes Israel for forsaking the true God.
Israel's army is strong, but Judah cries out to the LORD, the priests sound the trumpets, and God routs Israel.
Judah wins the victory by relying on God, capturing many of Israel's cities, and Jeroboam never again grows strong.
chapters.application: In the face of hardship, let us, like Abijah, first stand on God's promises, begin with prayer and worship, and trust that God will fight for us, for victory belongs to the LORD.

chapters.summary: After Abijah's death, Asa becomes king of Judah; he does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, removes the idols, and, relying on God, defeats the million-strong army of Zerah the Ethiopian.
keyPoints: Asa follows David's example in doing what is right, removing the foreign gods and the high places, and the land enjoys peace.
Asa cries out to God, relying on the name of the LORD, and defeats the vast Ethiopian army though greatly outnumbered.
Because Judah trusts in God, they win a great victory and carry off much plunder.
chapters.application: When we seek God wholeheartedly, remove the idols from our lives, and cry out to him in trouble, he will surely grant peace and victory.

chapters.summary: Encouraged by the prophet Azariah, King Asa removes the idols and leads the people to make a covenant with God, bringing peace and revival.
keyPoints: The prophet Azariah encourages Asa and the people of Judah, promising that whoever seeks God will surely find him.
Asa removes the idols throughout the land, repairs the altar, and leads the people to offer sacrifices to God and make a covenant.
The people of Judah rejoice over the covenant, and the land enjoys peace until Asa's later years.
chapters.application: When we seek God wholeheartedly and remove the idols from our lives, he will surely grant peace and blessing; let us act with courage and not shrink back because of circumstances.

chapters.summary: In his later years, because Asa relies on the king of Syria rather than on God, the prophet Hanani rebukes him; he finally falls ill and dies, and his life stands as a warning to later generations of both success and failure.
keyPoints: Asa forms an alliance with Ben-hadad king of Syria to attack Israel, without inquiring of the LORD.
The prophet Hanani rebukes Asa, pointing out that trusting in God is better than trusting in man, but Asa grows angry and has the prophet imprisoned.
In his later years Asa suffers a severe disease in his feet, and he seeks help only from physicians and not from the LORD; after his death he is buried in the city of David.
chapters.application: In good times and bad, let us rely wholeheartedly on God and not on the strength of man; let us hold fast to faith throughout our lives, until we see the Lord face to face.

chapters.summary: Jehoshaphat reveres God, abolishes idols, and teaches the people to keep the law; God establishes his kingdom, and he gains great honor and wealth.
keyPoints: Jehoshaphat walks in the early ways of David, seeking God and not worshiping Baal.
God establishes his kingdom; all Judah brings him tribute, and he gains great wealth and honor.
Jehoshaphat sends officials and Levites with the Book of the Law throughout the cities of Judah to teach the people.
chapters.application: Let us follow Jehoshaphat's example, honoring the Lord as supreme in our homes and daily lives, and diligently teaching God's word, so that our lives and all we influence may be blessed.

chapters.summary: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab to attack Ramoth-gilead, and by trusting the words of false prophets he falls into danger, but through Micaiah God makes the truth known and preserves Jehoshaphat.
keyPoints: Jehoshaphat becomes allied with Ahab by marriage and forms an alliance with him, compromising his relationship with God.
Four hundred false prophets tell Ahab what he wants to hear, but Micaiah alone proclaims God's true warning.
Ahab disguises himself for battle but is still struck down by an arrow and dies, while Jehoshaphat is kept safe by God.
chapters.application: When the voices around us all agree, let us seek God's will rather than follow the majority. God will surely protect those who fear him, even in the midst of danger.

chapters.summary: After being rebuked by a prophet, King Jehoshaphat reforms the justice system, appointing judges and urging them to fear the LORD and act with justice.
keyPoints: When Jehoshaphat returns to his palace, Jehu the seer rebukes him for allying with the wicked and provoking God's anger.
Jehoshaphat appoints judges throughout the land of Judah and charges them to judge righteously and take no bribes.
In Jerusalem he appoints Levites and priests as a supreme court to handle difficult cases.
chapters.application: In daily life, let us treat others with reverence for God, pursue justice, keep far from ill-gotten gain, and let God's righteousness be seen in every decision we make.

chapters.summary: Facing the combined attack of Moab, Ammon, and the people of Mount Seir, Jehoshaphat leads Judah in fasting and prayer, trusts God for victory, and the enemy armies destroy one another.
keyPoints: Facing a powerful enemy, Jehoshaphat resolves to seek God and proclaims a fast throughout the nation.
In the temple, Jehoshaphat prays, acknowledging God's great power and asking him to judge their enemies.
Through Jahaziel God promises victory; the people trust and sing praises, and the enemy armies turn on and destroy each other.
chapters.application: In the face of hardship, let us first pray and seek God, trust his promises, and replace worry with praise, and we will experience his salvation.

chapters.summary: After Jehoram becomes king he does evil; God pronounces judgment through Elijah, and the Philistines and others attack him; Jehoram falls ill and dies, and no one mourns him.
keyPoints: Jehoram follows the evil ways of the house of Ahab, kills his own brothers, marries Ahab's daughter, and leads Judah into idolatry.
Elijah writes a letter warning Jehoram and prophesying disaster, because he has forsaken God and brought suffering on the people.
God stirs up the Philistines and the Arabians against him; Jehoram is struck with a severe disease, his bowels come out, and he dies with no one mourning him.
chapters.application: Let us keep far from wickedness and heed God's word. Even in adversity, let us repent and turn back to God, for he is merciful, yet his judgment is not to be treated lightly.

chapters.summary: Ahaziah becomes king of Judah and does evil, allying himself with Joram king of Israel; he is finally killed by Jehu, and his mother Athaliah usurps the throne.
keyPoints: Ahaziah follows the evil ways of the house of Ahab, and disaster comes upon him because of his friendship with Joram.
After Ahaziah is killed, his mother Athaliah destroys the royal family and usurps the throne of Judah.
God preserves the house of David, and Jehoshabeath hides Joash away, continuing the line of David.
chapters.application: Let us be careful in choosing our companions and keep far from wickedness; even when circumstances seem dark, God remains faithful to keep his promises, and we should trust him and not be afraid.

chapters.summary: In the seventh year, the priest Jehoiada makes Joash king and destroys the usurper Athaliah, restoring the throne to the house of David.
keyPoints: Jehoiada makes a covenant with the commanders and installs Joash as king.
The people guard the temple, Joash is anointed, and the crowd shouts for joy.
Athaliah is put to death, and the throne is restored to the house of David.
chapters.application: When wickedness seems to have the upper hand, God will surely act according to his promises. Let us stay faithful to God's covenant, stand courageously on the side of righteousness, and trust that he will keep and accomplish his purpose.

chapters.summary: While the priest Jehoiada is alive, King Joash does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, but after Jehoiada's death he forsakes God and is finally killed by his own servants.
keyPoints: Joash comes to the throne as a boy, and under Jehoiada's guidance repairs the temple and restores worship.
After Jehoiada dies, Joash listens to the officials of Judah, forsakes the LORD, and serves idols.
God sends prophets to warn him, but Joash will not listen, and even puts Jehoiada's son Zechariah to death.
chapters.application: Let us keep a thankful heart always, never forgetting God's grace just because circumstances change; let us hold fast to the true faith until we see the Lord face to face.

chapters.summary: Amaziah king of Judah does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, but his heart is not wholly true; because of pride he goes to war against Israel, is defeated, and is finally killed by conspirators.
keyPoints: At first Amaziah follows God's ways, but his heart is not wholly true, and he does not fully remove the idols.
Relying on his army's strength he defeats Edom, but he brings their idols back and worships them, provoking God's anger.
Because of pride he challenges Israel, is defeated and captured, and is later betrayed and killed, coming to a tragic end.
chapters.application: Let us follow the Lord with a wholehearted devotion, never growing proud or complacent, but relying on God with humility, lest a moment of success cause us to fall.

chapters.summary: King Uzziah grows proud and unlawfully burns incense in the temple, and God punishes him with leprosy, so that he is cut off from the LORD for the rest of his life.
keyPoints: Uzziah does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, following the example of his father Amaziah, and the nation grows strong.
Because of his strength he becomes proud, and presumes to enter the temple to burn incense, encroaching on the priest's office.
God strikes him with leprosy, and he is forced to live in isolation until the day he dies.
chapters.application: Let us keep to our own place and never grow proud because of success; let us humbly submit to God, respect his order, lest we lose his presence and blessing.

chapters.summary: Jotham becomes king of Judah and does what is right in the eyes of the LORD; because he fears God, the nation grows strong and he defeats the Ammonites.
keyPoints: Jotham follows the example of his father Uzziah in doing what is right, but he does not enter the temple of the LORD, and the people still act corruptly.
He builds the upper gate of the house of the LORD and strengthens the cities of Judah.
He wages war against the Ammonites and defeats them, receiving tribute from them for three years, and the nation grows strong.
chapters.application: Let us follow Jotham's example, holding fast to what is right in the ordinary course of life; fearing God will surely bring his blessing and presence.

chapters.summary: King Ahaz does evil, and God allows Judah to be defeated by Syria and Israel; the prophet Oded urges the Israelites to release the captives from Judah, but Ahaz continues to sin and finally suffers the consequences of his own actions.
keyPoints: Ahaz follows the ways of the kings of Israel, casts images of Baal, and does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD.
God hands Judah over to Syria and Israel, and Judah suffers a crushing defeat, with many carried away captive.
The prophet Oded urges the Israelites to release the captives from Judah, but Ahaz continues to do evil, appeals to Assyria for help, and in the end brings disaster on himself.
chapters.application: When we stray from God, let us watch and turn back, rather than sinning more and more against him amid our troubles, as Ahaz did.

chapters.summary: After Hezekiah becomes king, he cleanses the temple, restores worship, and leads the people of Judah to return to God.
keyPoints: In the first year of his reign, Hezekiah assembles the priests and Levites and commands them to cleanse the temple.
The priests and Levites spend eight days cleansing the temple, removing all that is unclean.
After the cleansing, sin offerings and burnt offerings are presented, restoring worship in the temple.
chapters.application: Let us examine our hearts, remove sin, and once again make God the center of our lives, restoring intimate fellowship with him.

chapters.summary: King Hezekiah calls the whole nation to Jerusalem to keep the Passover; God heals the hearts of the people, bringing them into one accord, and great joy and blessing follow.
keyPoints: King Hezekiah invites the people of both the northern and southern kingdoms to keep the Passover together, showing his desire for unity.
God moves the hearts of the people, leading them to humble themselves, repent, and come to the temple to keep the feast.
The people keep the feast for seven days, then joyfully keep it for seven more, rejoicing greatly and receiving God's blessing.
chapters.application: When we are willing to set aside our differences and seek God's will, he will surely grant unity and joy. Lord, help us humbly turn back to you and experience your healing and grace.

chapters.summary: After cleansing the temple, Hezekiah leads the people to keep the Passover and restores the duties of the priests and Levites, bringing the people back to God.
keyPoints: Hezekiah orders the high places and idols torn down, cleansing the whole land of Judah and Benjamin.
The people give willingly of their firstfruits and tithes, providing for the needs of the priests and Levites.
Hezekiah establishes the divisions so that the priests and Levites each fulfill their duties in serving in the temple.
chapters.application: Let us cleanse ourselves from within, remove every idol, give with a thankful heart, and serve God faithfully, putting our faith into practice in daily life.

chapters.summary: Facing the threat of Sennacherib king of Assyria, Hezekiah trusts God and encourages the people; God sends an angel to defeat the Assyrian army, and Hezekiah is delivered and cared for by God.
keyPoints: Hezekiah prepares the city's defenses and encourages the people to trust in God, not to fear the threats of the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib king of Assyria blasphemes God, and God sends an angel who strikes down a hundred and eighty-five thousand men of the Assyrian army.
After Hezekiah recovers from his illness he grows proud, but he humbles himself and repents, and God forgives him and blesses Judah.
chapters.application: In the face of hardship, let us, like Hezekiah, first seek God, entrust ourselves to him in faith and prayer, for he will surely watch over us; and let us guard against pride after success, keeping a humble and thankful heart always.

chapters.summary: King Manasseh does evil and provokes God's anger; he is carried captive to Babylon, and after he repents he is restored, yet he is never able to fully remove the idols, and after his death Amon succeeds him and continues in evil.
keyPoints: Manasseh follows the detestable practices of the nations, rebuilds the high places, and worships idols, provoking God's anger.
God punishes Manasseh through the king of Assyria; in his distress he earnestly seeks God, deeply repents, and is granted mercy.
Though Manasseh removes the idols, Amon repeats the same sins, and is finally killed by his own servants, and his son Josiah succeeds him.
chapters.application: However rebellious we have been, if we truly repent, God will hear us. May we never repeat the same mistakes, but live each day in reverence for God.

chapters.summary: During the reign of King Josiah, idols are removed, the temple is repaired, the Book of the Law is discovered, and he leads the people to make a covenant with God and restore the Passover.
keyPoints: Josiah comes to the throne at age eight and reigns thirty-one years, doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
He cleanses Judah and Jerusalem, tears down the altars of idols, and breaks the carved images to pieces.
While the temple is being repaired, the Book of the Law is discovered; when the king hears it read, he tears his clothes and humbly seeks God.
chapters.application: Let us take God's word as the standard for our lives, receive it with humility, turn back to him promptly, and lead our families and society to walk in the right path.

chapters.summary: King Josiah keeps the Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, arranges the service of the priests and Levites, reaffirms the law, and leads the people back to God.
keyPoints: Josiah commands the people to keep the Passover and offer sacrifices to God according to the Book of the Law.
The priests and Levites are arranged by their divisions to serve in the temple.
Josiah and the leaders give generously of the sacrificial animals, and the people keep the feast together in one accord.
chapters.application: May we, like Josiah, earnestly obey God's word, serve faithfully in our families and churches, lead others to turn to the Lord, and delight in walking with God.

chapters.summary: The last kings of Judah, one after another, are carried into exile because of their rebellion against God; the temple is destroyed and the people are removed to Babylon, until Cyrus king of Persia issues a decree to rebuild the temple.
keyPoints: Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah reign one after another, each doing evil, leading the nation into decline.
Zedekiah rebels against Babylon, and the priests and the people also sin greatly, provoking God's wrath.
The temple is destroyed and the people are carried into exile, fulfilling the words of the prophets, until the time of Cyrus king of Persia.
chapters.application: Let us keep far from sin and humbly submit to God; even amid discipline, let us trust in his promises and the grace of restoration.
